subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: When a flat plane slices through a solid, the flat region where the plane meets the solid is called the cross section. A slice taken parallel to a face of a right rectangular prism makes a cross section that is the same size and shape as that face. A slice taken parallel to the base of a pyramid makes a smaller figure with the same shape as the base.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $6$ cm long, $4$ cm wide, and $3$ cm tall. A plane slices the prism parallel to its top and bottom faces. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?

steps: A slice parallel to a face of a prism produces a cross section congruent to that face.
The top and bottom faces are the $6$ cm by $4$ cm faces, which are rectangles.
So the cross section is a rectangle.

items.prompt: Using the same prism that is $6$ cm long, $4$ cm wide, and $3$ cm tall, a plane slices it parallel to the top and bottom faces. What are the dimensions of the cross section?

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
The top and bottom faces measure $6$ cm by $4$ cm.
The cross section is $6$ cm by $4$ cm.

items.prompt: A cube has edges that are each $5$ in long. A plane slices the cube parallel to one of its faces. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
Every face of a cube is a square with side $5$ in.
So the cross section is a square.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $8$ in by $8$ in by $2$ in. A plane slices it parallel to one of the $8$ in by $8$ in faces. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section, and what are its dimensions?
items.answer: A square that is $8$ in by $8$ in

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
The $8$ in by $8$ in face has two equal sides, so it is a square.
The cross section is a square measuring $8$ in by $8$ in.

items.prompt: A box is shaped like a right rectangular prism that is $10$ cm long, $7$ cm wide, and $5$ cm tall. A plane slices it parallel to the $10$ cm by $5$ cm face. What are the dimensions of the cross section?

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
The face described measures $10$ cm by $5$ cm.
The cross section is $10$ cm by $5$ cm.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $9$ m by $3$ m by $3$ m. A plane slices it parallel to a $3$ m by $3$ m face. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
The $3$ m by $3$ m face has two equal sides, so it is a square.
The cross section is a square.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $12$ cm by $5$ cm by $4$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the $5$ cm by $4$ cm face. Is the cross section a square or a rectangle that is not a square? Explain by giving its dimensions.
items.answer: A rectangle that is not a square, measuring $5$ cm by $4$ cm

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
The face measures $5$ cm by $4$ cm.
Because $5 \neq 4$, the two sides are unequal, so it is a rectangle that is not a square.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $7$ cm by $4$ cm by $4$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the $7$ cm by $4$ cm face. Find the area of the cross section.

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face, so the cross section is $7$ cm by $4$ cm.
Area of a rectangle is length times width: $7 \times 4 = 28$.
The area of the cross section is $28 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $6$ cm by $5$ cm by $2$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the $6$ cm by $5$ cm face. Find the area of the cross section.

steps: The cross section is congruent to the $6$ cm by $5$ cm face.
Area is length times width: $6 \times 5 = 30$.
The area of the cross section is $30 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a rectangular base that is $10$ ft by $6$ ft. A plane slices the pyramid parallel to the base. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?

steps: A slice parallel to the base of a pyramid has the same shape as the base.
The base is a rectangle, so the cross section is also a rectangle.
It is smaller than the base, but it is still a rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a square base that is $8$ cm by $8$ cm. A plane slices the pyramid parallel to the base. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?

steps: A slice parallel to the base of a pyramid has the same shape as the base.
The base is a square, so the cross section is also a square.
It is a smaller square than the base.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $10$ ft by $6$ ft. A plane slices it parallel to the base, exactly halfway up the height. Each side length of the cross section is half the matching base side. What are the dimensions of the cross section?

steps: A base-parallel slice halfway up has side lengths that are half of the base side lengths.
Half of $10$ ft is $5$ ft, and half of $6$ ft is $3$ ft.
The cross section measures $5$ ft by $3$ ft.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a square base $12$ in by $12$ in. A plane slices it parallel to the base, halfway up the height, where each side length is half the base side. What are the dimensions of the cross section?

steps: A base-parallel slice halfway up has side lengths that are half of the base side lengths.
Half of $12$ in is $6$ in for each side.
The cross section measures $6$ in by $6$ in.

items.prompt: True or false: When a plane slices a right rectangular prism parallel to one of its faces, the cross section is the same shape and size as that face. Explain.

steps: A slicing plane parallel to a face stays the same distance from that face all across the cut.
This makes the cross section congruent to the face it is parallel to.
So the statement is true: the cross section matches that face in shape and size.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $9$ cm by $4$ cm by $4$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to a $4$ cm by $4$ cm face. Find both the shape and the area of the cross section.

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face, which is $4$ cm by $4$ cm.
Because the two sides are equal, the cross section is a square.
Its area is $4 \times 4 = 16$, so the area is $16 \text{ cm}^2$.
